domain: Gun Violence Incident Reporting and Analysis
scenario:
A national public safety organization is developing an enterprise-level Gun Violence Incident Reporting and Analysis System. This system aims to collect, store, and analyze data related to gun violence incidents across the United States. It will support law enforcement agencies, policymakers, and researchers by providing detailed insights into gun violence patterns, victim demographics, and geographic hot spots.

The system will track incidents by date, location (state, city or county, and specific address), and the number of casualties (killed and injured). Additionally, it should also allow for the classification of incidents based on various factors such as the type of firearm used, the motive, and any gang-related activity.

The platform needs to support complex queries and reports, enabling users to analyze trends over time, identify high-risk areas, and evaluate the effectiveness of gun control measures. It should also facilitate the integration of operations data, such as emergency response actions taken during or after incidents.

Advanced user roles and permissions are required to manage access to sensitive information, ensuring that only authorized personnel can view or modify certain data. The system must also include robust data visualization tools to help stakeholders understand the data through maps, charts, and dashboards.
